name: ToothFairy
size: 443 volumes (443 patients; 153 with dense and sparse annotations; 290 with sparse annotations only; plus 50 hidden test volumes not released)
notes: Annotations: 3D binary voxel masks of the inferior alveolar canal (1 class); sparse 1-voxel-thin canal path (gt_sparse.npy) for all 443, dense alpha-shape masks (gt_alpha.npy) for 153; the raw DICOM download has sparse annotations only. | Formats: NumPy .npy (data.npy in Hounsfield units; avg shape 169x342x370) plus a separate raw DICOM download; splits.json (training / validation / test / synthetic groups; 'synthetic' = sparse-only volumes; these are the authors' internal splits, not the challenge test set); README.md. | No patient clinical data provided (structured challenge description). Scanner (dataset level): NewTom/NTVGiMK4, 3 mA, 110 kV, 0.3 mm cubic voxels. Number of cases in the DICOM download not confirmed. MICCAI 2023 challenge (https://toothfairy.grand-challenge.org/). Extends the earlier Maxillo dataset. License comes only from the grand-challenge dataset page; the ditto page states none and the version is unspecified. Official challenge test set: 50 volumes, never released (structured challenge description), acquired on a different scanner (i-CAT, 0.4 mm voxels). Paper published 2025 (online Dec 2024) but release was 2023. Ditto page also asks to cite IEEE Access 2024 (https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2024.3408629) and CVPR 2022 (https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR52688.2022.02046); grand-challenge page misprints the IEEE Access DOI as 10.1109/ACCESS.2022.3144840. Code: https://github.com/AImageLab-zip/ToothFairy (MIT; code only).

name: ToothFairy2
size: 480 volumes (Set A 417; Set B 63; plus 50 hidden test volumes not released)
notes: Annotations: dense 3D multi-class voxel label maps, 42 classes (jaws; inferior alveolar canals; maxillary sinus; pharynx; bridges; crowns; implants; upper and lower teeth incl. wisdom teeth; tooth IDs use FDI notation) for all 480 public volumes. | Formats: MHA (.mha), Hounsfield units, 0.3 mm isotropic; nnU-Net layout with dataset.json (label map). | No patient clinical data provided (structured challenge description). An official split is mentioned but no split file confirmed. MICCAI 2024 challenge (https://toothfairy2.grand-challenge.org/). Set A (417) overlaps ToothFairy volumes (443, so not all are included) but adds annotations; Set B is new. Last dataset update 2024-07-07. Dataset first introduced in a CVPR 2025 paper (https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.00494); paper_url is the MedIA challenge paper. License comes only from the grand-challenge page and the version is unspecified; ditto page shows no license.

name: ToothFairy3
size: 532 volumes (Set A 417; Set B 63; Set C 52; plus 50 hidden test volumes not released; 582 total per paper)
notes: Annotations: dense 3D multi-class voxel label maps, 77 classes (FDI teeth; 32 pulp cavities; incisive and lingual canals; jaws; IAC; etc.) for all 532 public volumes; the interactive IAC task adds 3D click coordinates (5 per canal branch; whether training clicks are in the download not confirmed). | Formats: NIfTI (.nii.gz), Hounsfield units, 0.3 mm; nnU-Net layout (images/labels) with dataset.json; non-standard RPI orientation (official fix_orientation.py converts). | No patient clinical data provided (ODIN2025 structured document); paper says age/sex/year were retained internally for split construction, distribution not confirmed. An official split is mentioned but no split file confirmed. ToothFairy3 challenge in the ODIN2025 cluster at MICCAI 2025 (https://toothfairy3.grand-challenge.org/). Tasks: multi-class segmentation and interactive IAC segmentation. Sets A and B overlap ToothFairy2; Set C (52) is new. Scanner conflict: ditto page says Set C was acquired with a different machine; ODIN2025 document and paper say all public data come from NewTom/NTVGiMK4. Class-count conflict: GitHub ToothFairy3/README.md says 45 classes vs 77 elsewhere. Dataset paper: MICCAI 2026 LNCS chapter (DOI found via Crossref 2026-10-23); also UNIMORE IRIS handle https://hdl.handle.net/11380/1405369 (author PDF embargoed until 2027-10-31). Paper abstract says 102 additional scans over ToothFairy2 while ditto page says 52 new volumes (102 likely = 52 public + 50 test; unconfirmed).

name: ToothFairy4
size: 625 volumes + 1001 reports per language (Italian; English) (625 patients; 250 cases with 1 report; 371 with 2; 3 with 3; plus 50 hidden test cases not released)
notes: Annotations: free-text clinician reports as targets (1-3 per case; Italian originals + English translations by an LLM pipeline using gpt-5.2, only partly checked by clinicians); no segmentation masks included (P/F/S labels can be reused from ToothFairy3; mind the volume orientation). | Formats: NIfTI (.nii.gz), one volume per case in cbct/; reports in reports_it/ and reports_en/ (English confirmed .txt; Italian file format not confirmed). | No other context, gender or medical history provided (ODIN2026 document). Scanners at dataset level: NewTom; Planmeca Viso G7; Planmeca ProMax; Sirona XG3D; SOREDEX Cranex 3D; de Gotzen; Carestream CS 8100 3D. An official split is mentioned but no split file confirmed. ODIN 2026 Task 1 at MICCAI 2026 (https://odin2026.grand-challenge.org/): CBCT-to-report generation for implant and surgical planning. Multicenter: sets P (417) / F (63) / S (52) come from ToothFairy3 and set A (100) is new from the Digital Research Center of Sfax on different scanners (not 0.3 mm isotropic). Size conflict: ditto states 625 but the subsets sum to 632 and reports-per-case counts sum to 624; the ODIN page says 630 training volumes; the ODIN2026 document says 630 patients. Hidden external test set of 50 cases. No dedicated dataset paper found; ditto cites a MICCAI 2026 ontology-reporting paper (https://hdl.handle.net/11380/1411068; describes 893 reports for 529 ToothFairy3 volumes, likely an earlier subset) plus the ToothFairy2 MedIA and ToothFairy TMI papers. ODIN 2026 Zenodo document (https://zenodo.org/records/19727377) is CC BY 4.0 but covers the document only.

name: AlphaDent
size: 1455 photos (1320 labeled train/valid photos from 295 patients; 135 test photos with hidden labels)
notes: Annotations: YOLO instance-segmentation polygons (TXT, one file per image), 9 classes (abrasion; filling; crown; caries grades 1-6), train/valid only (1320 photos); test labels hidden (Kaggle leaderboard). | Formats: JPG photos (Canon 6D Mark II with intraoral mirror; most above 5000x3000; frontal and chewing-surface views); TXT polygon labels; yolo_seg_train.yaml class map; split by folders (train 1237 / valid 83 / test 135). No PNG masks in the Zenodo / Hugging Face / GitHub zip although the paper's directory tree lists them; Kaggle contents not confirmed. | Patient sex and age are encoded in train/valid filenames (e.g. p002_F_52_001.jpg); test filenames carry none. Filenames give 293 patients (162 F; 131 M), matching the paper's 131 male + 162 female but not its stated 295. Also on Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/alpha-dent/data; account needed; terms not checked), Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ZFTurbo/AlphaDent; lists apache-2.0; identical zip) and GitHub release v1.1 (https://github.com/ZFTurbo/AlphaDent; code Apache-2.0). Paper counts conflict: abstract says over 1200 images; methods say 1320 train/valid + 135 test; directory listing says 121 test; 1455 matches the Hugging Face row count and the zip listing. Preprint arXiv:2507.22512.

name: SMART-OM
notes: Annotations: VIA JSON polygons at 3 levels (region / full tissue / lesion; lesion level not for Normal), region labels mapped via Descriptor XLSX files (labels not inside the JSON); image-level class (normal / variation from normal / OPMD / oral cancer) and anatomical site (8 oral regions) from folder structure; unannotated copies included. | Formats: JPEG/JPG photos (8 PNG, all oral cancer; smartphones Samsung Galaxy M15 and Apple iPhone 14, per-image device not confirmed); VIA JSON; XLSX descriptors; XLSX patient metadata. | Patient metadata XLSX (2 sheets): demographics and personal history (age; sex; tobacco smoking and chewing; areca nut; alcohol, each with frequency/duration/status/start age; brushing habits; family, medical and dental history; denture use) and clinical findings (status of ~50 intraoral sites; lesion location, color, margin, surface, description, size, pain, classification). Metadata has 325 patient rows vs 331 subjects stated. Same images repeated across annotation-level folders (7699 image files in zip). No train/test splits. Data license CC-BY-4.0 per Figshare; the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Validation code: https://github.com/Anwesh2000/SMART_OM_Dataset_Technical_Validation. Not to be confused with the earlier 'SMART Intraoral images Dataset' (1850 images / 235 patients) on India's AIKOSH portal from the same group.

name: Bite2Text
data_type: 3D intraoral scan + 2D intraoral photo + text report
size: 2000 scans + 5000 photos + 2403 reports (1000 patients; upper and lower scan per patient; 5 photos per patient; plus 50 hidden test cases not released)
notes: Annotations: clinician free-text orthodontic reports for the scans and for the photos (Italian original + English translation); a template-structured version (generated by gpt-5-latest, clinician-reviewed; 'a derived annotation layer') is described in the paper but its distribution is not confirmed; at least 2 reports per patient; no segmentation labels. | Formats: STL meshes (registered upper/lower, RAS frame, bases removed, avg 114096 vertices; scanners incl. Carestream and 3Shape TRIOS) in ios/; photos in intraoral-photo/ (5 views: frontal, left buccal, right buccal, upper occlusal, lower occlusal; avg 3926x2545, cropped and rotated; file format not confirmed); reports in reports_ios_it/, reports_ios_en/, reports_intraoral-photo_it/, reports_intraoral-photo_en/ (file format not confirmed). | Photos and meshes are stripped of metadata; no demographics distributed (paper gives cohort stats only: age 16-99, ~58% female). Paper: 'Do Multimodal LLMs Understand Intraoral Dental Data? Dataset Platform and Baselines' (ECCV 2026); no DOI/arXiv found, paper_url is the PDF on the senior author's site (index: https://federicobolelli.it/pages/all-pubs.html#2026ECCV_bite2text). Code: https://github.com/AImageLab-zip/IOS-Report. LICENSE CONFLICT: dataset page and ODIN page say CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 but the paper says CC BY-SA 4.0. Used as ODIN 2026 Task 2 with 50 hidden test cases (not released). ODIN page showed 2000 patient cases struck out and corrected to 1000. Paper labels this an initial release; platform designed for continuous expansion. Whether hidden test cases are among the 1000 is unclear (ODIN table suggests separate). Download needs an account and was not tested.

name: CariesXrays
size: 6000 radiographs (5380 patients; 13783 caries instances; train 4800; test 1200)
notes: Annotations: Pascal VOC XML bounding boxes, single class 'Decay'; 13785 boxes in the released XML (paper: 13783 in abstract, 13778 in statistics section). | Formats: JPEG, 3-channel, native ~2648x1280 or 2440x1280 (paper says images were resized to 1333x800; not true for the released files); Pascal VOC XML; no split files (XML <folder> field 'img' 5208 / 'test' 792 does not match the paper's 4800/1200, so not a split). | No per-image metadata (paper shows aggregate age/gender only). Paper train/test split 4800/1200 (random). Full data on a public personal Google Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qWL2f0A-vf91StHxs24eoiFDyuoHEh4N; Annotations.zip and JPEGImages.zip dated 10/20/24) linked from the GitHub README; repo itself holds a 0.5% sample (50 images in a misspelled 'JEPGImages' folder + 50 XML). No data license stated anywhere. An earlier repo (SCNU-BMI/AAAI2024-CariesXrays) promised 'a license that allows free usage for research purposes' but none was published; data was not public at publication and the Drive link was added later. 5563 of the 6000 filenames also appear in OralXrays-9 (same group); whether they are the same images is not confirmed. Not the same as CariXray.

name: OralXrays-9
size: 12688 radiographs (11480 patients; 84113 annotated instances; train 10000; test 2688)
notes: Annotations: COCO JSON bounding boxes, 9 classes (apical periodontitis; dental caries ('Decay'); wisdom teeth; missing teeth; dental fillings; root canal fillings; dental implants; porcelain crowns; ceramic bridges); 65494 train + 18639 test; the 'segmentation' field is only the 4 bbox corners (no masks); 31 train annotations have undefined category_id 0. | Formats: JPEG 1991x1127, 3-channel (paper says resized to 1333x800; not true for the released files); COCO JSON (instances_train2017.json / instances_val2017.json); AES-encrypted zips. | Split: train2017 (10000) / val2017 (2688 = the paper's test set), patient-level. Annotation totals sum to 84133 not the stated 84113. Images were extracted from DICOM per the supplement; DICOM not distributed. No per-image metadata. Hosted on Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_y7ERcFicnOYY2DMR6Qe1W4KGdCsoQ1n); password is published in the official GitHub README, but README.md inside the Drive folder says 'please contact us to request the password' (confirmed 2026-10-23). No data license stated. Binz-Chen/CVPR2025_OralXrays-9 is a 2026 fork of the original Binz-Chan repo; co-author repo: https://github.com/XiaochengFang/CVPR2025_OralXrays-9. A 2026 paper (arXiv 2603.28297) reportedly uses it for instance segmentation, but the official release has only bounding boxes.

name: DENTEX
size: 3903 radiographs (693 quadrant-only; 634 quadrant and tooth number; 1005 fully labeled with diagnosis; 1571 unlabeled)
notes: Annotations: per-tooth polygons + bounding boxes with hierarchical labels: quadrant (categories_1) -> tooth number (categories_2) -> diagnosis (categories_3: caries; deep caries; periapical lesion; impacted); polygons confirmed in all train/validation label files; test ground truth is LabelMe JSON polygons with 8 raw Turkish label codes (1-çürük; 2-küretaj; 6-gömülü; 3-kanal; 0-saglam; 7-lezyon; 5-çekim; 8-kırık), no official mapping to the 4 published classes found; 1571 images unlabeled (pre-training). | Formats: PNG X-rays (sizes vary, e.g. 2872x1504, 1976x976); COCO-style JSON (train/val); LabelMe JSON (test); validation_triple.json on Hugging Face only. | No per-image metadata (cohort: patients aged 12 and above). MICCAI 2023 challenge dataset (https://dentex.grand-challenge.org/). Fully labeled set split 705 train / 50 val / 250 test; test was hidden during the challenge but all ground truth is now on Hugging Face (Zenodo v1 2023 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7812323 has only training+validation). License conflict: HF card and DENTEX GitHub say CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; Zenodo record says CC-BY-4.0; HierarchicalDet README says CC BY-SA 4.0; arXiv v2 says CC-BY. Same data as HierarchicalDet method paper (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-43987-2_38; arXiv 2303.06500), so not catalogued separately. Provenance conflict: grand-challenge says three institutions with varying equipment; arXiv v2 and HierarchicalDet describe a single VistaPano S unit (v2: three hospitals in Turkiye).

name: DenPAR
notes: Annotations: tooth segmentation masks (per radiograph PNG; per tooth PNG + COCO, single class 'tooth', no per-tooth FDI label); CEJ and apex keypoints plus per-tooth bounding boxes (derived from masks) in per-image JSON; alveolar crestal bone-level polylines (per-image JSON + COCO polygons, class 'bone'). | Formats: JPG radiographs (e.g. 1168x886); PNG masks; JSON (custom + COCO); XLSX metadata. | Metadata XLSX 'Characteristics of radiographs included.xlsx': 1000 rows with id, Arch (upper/lower), Site (right/left/anterior), FDI notation of visible teeth. Paper says each image is accompanied by age and sex metadata, but the released files have no age/sex (aggregate only: 440 male, 560 female). No device info. Official splits by folder: train 650 / validation 150 / test 200 (tooth-wise masks 2882 / 655 / 864). Intraoral periapical (IOPA) radiographs from Dental Hospital Peradeniya Sri Lanka (2020-2023), curated for alveolar bone loss detection. Zenodo record has earlier restricted versions dated 2024 (13998619; 14181645); first open version 2025-07-31. dataset_url is a version DOI. Article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 but dataset is CC BY 4.0.

name: PRAD
notes: Annotations: pixel-level segmentation, 9 classes (tooth; alveolar bone; pulp; root canal filling; denture crown; dental fillings; implant; orthodontic devices; apical periodontitis), annotated with Labelme, for the 5000 released images; image-level multi-label classification (periodontitis; apical periodontitis; inadequate root canal filling) described in paper but 'coming soon' in repo. | Formats: not confirmed (data only via application; repo holds no data files). | No metadata confirmed; data from a hospital endodontics department. Paper split 80/20 random; released split unknown. Paper calls it PRAD-10K (10000 periapical radiographs). Only 5000 images with segmentation labels are released via emailed signed application to aics@nankai.edu.cn (~14 working days); open for application since 2025-09-20. License conflict: README shows CC BY-NC badge but footer says 'All rights reserved' and application terms forbid redistribution/modification/commercial use; no LICENSE file. arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07760. Upgraded PRAD++ (IEEE TMI 2026) and MM-PRAD (multimodal with textual descriptions, under development) announced; release details unknown.

name: CariXray
notes: Annotations: single class 'caries'; bounding boxes and instance polygons in YOLO Darknet format (COCO conversion scripts provided); on-Drive label layout not confirmed. | Formats: YOLO Darknet txt labels; image format not confirmed (Drive inaccessible). | Images collected from publicly available sources (data availability statement cites Roboflow Universe, Kaggle, Zenodo and Mendeley Data entries) and labeled/validated by dental experts. Data on Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14Km_y3JvuJesQtbDPFqSZhu2Zgv7xzS9) linked from the GitHub repo; anonymous access returned a Google sign-in page/HTTP 401 on 2026-10-23; a separate sample-subset Drive folder is also inaccessible. GitHub repo contains scripts only (inter-rater, 5-fold split tool, YOLO-to-COCO converters); its yolo2coco_detection/tutorial images (door photos; classes chair/handle/table/button/person) are unrelated third-party sample data. Repo code is Apache-2.0; README says 'open license for research and educational purposes' with no specific data license. Upstream source licenses unknown. Paper online 2025-12-29 (Machine Vision and Applications 37(1) art. 20, 2026). Size from search-engine abstract snippet only (paper paywalled). Not the same as panoramic CariesXrays.

name: Teeth3DS
size: 1800 scans (900 patients; 23999 annotated teeth; official split 1200 train / 600 test)
notes: Annotations: per-vertex FDI tooth labels (0 = gingiva) and per-vertex tooth instance IDs in one JSON per scan (keys id_patient, jaw, labels, instances), all 1800 scans. | Formats: OBJ meshes (trimesh export; vertex colours are a constant grey placeholder, checked in 2 files); JSON labels; TXT split lists; license.txt. STL raw scans shown in the v1 paper are not distributed. | No per-scan metadata (paper aggregates only: scanners Primescan / Trios3 / iTero Element 2 Plus; 50% orthodontic / 50% prosthetic; 50% male; ~70% under 16). Also the dataset of the MICCAI 2022 3DTeethSeg22 challenge (challenge paper: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2305.18277; challenge split train 1200 scans / 16004 teeth, test 600 scans / 7995 teeth). Upper and lower jaws scanned separately. Two splits on OSF: challenge split and official Teeth3DS split. Test set was hidden during the challenge and released afterwards. Challenge paper says Figshare but no Figshare record found; repo README links only OSF. No standalone copy: data_part_1 to 6 of the Teeth3DS+ OSF project. Commercial use needs a separate license (contact@udini.ai). Dataset repo (renamed): https://github.com/abenhamadou/3DTeethSeg_MICCAI_Challenges. Grand-challenge page (https://3dteethseg.grand-challenge.org/) no longer maintained.

name: Teeth3DS+
size: 1800 scans (over 900 patients; 23999 annotated teeth; 340 scans with landmarks from 170 patients; 30536 landmarks)
notes: Annotations: segmentation JSON as in Teeth3DS for 1800 scans; 3D landmark coordinates in __kpt.json files (6 classes: Cusp; Mesial; Distal; OuterPoint; InnerPoint; FacialPoint) on 340 scans / 30536 points (train 240 files / 21394 points; test 100 files / 9142 points); the 100 landmark-test scans have no segmentation labels. | Formats: OBJ meshes; JSON (segmentation labels; __kpt.json landmarks); TXT split lists (Teeth3DS, 3DTeethSeg22 and 3DTeethLand splits); license.txt. | No per-scan metadata (aggregate scanner counts in the 3DTeethLand paper only). OSF also has a Teeth3DS_sample component (1 OBJ + label JSON + kpt JSON) for quick tests. Superset of Teeth3DS built for the MICCAI 2024 3DTeethLand challenge (challenge paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08323). Paper lists tasks: tooth detection, segmentation, labeling, 3D modeling, landmark identification. Shares the arXiv ID 2210.06094 with Teeth3DS (v2 Nov 2024; v3 Jan 2026). Data on OSF https://osf.io/xctdy/ (landmarks: https://osf.io/um96h/, public, no login). File count on OSF: 1900 scans = 1800 original + 100 landmark-test scans in data_part_7, from 68 patient IDs not in Teeth3DS (conflicts with the paper's 340 landmark scans from 170 patients all within the segmentation set). Landmark test labels were hidden during the challenge but are now on OSF. Landing page links osf.io/um96h text to osf.io/xctdy and its 3DTeethSeg paper link points to 2210.06094. License history: README briefly said CC BY-SA 4.0 (2023-06-08) before CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; website footer CC BY-SA 4.0 refers to the website; commercial-license wording added 2026-10-21. Commercial use needs a separate license (contact@udini.ai).
